data.narrative:
Long Wall is a late-stage Defense & Security company founded by executives with prior SpaceX and Morgan Stanley experience. The company has raised $544M to date. The comparable universe includes 10 private peers (Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems among them) and 2 public comps (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS), though a tight peer set at identical stage and valuation tier remains limited.

Stage-progression analysis, applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage advancement, yields $653M from the $544M raised proxy. The peer-median method is not applicable here; while 21 same-sector peers exist across the Defense & Security universe, the intersection of same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier criteria produced fewer than three datapoints, making a narrow median unreliable. A broader cross-sector median would introduce material noise.

The triangulated range derived from stage-progression alone spans $555M (low), $653M (median), and $751M (high). This single-method result should be weighted with caution given the limited comparable datapoints. Key uncertainties include the scarcity of late-stage private comps in defense tech, the absence of recent exit multiples for the sector, and the bespoke nature of defense-contracting economics. Revenue trajectory, contract backlog, and customer concentration would strengthen any refined analysis.
